page.layout: One page of text: at the top a poem of Theodore Beza's title, set in full width; below a rule, a heading and a second poem in verse, full width. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: THEOD. BEZÆ
main_text.p: En tibi nunc prodit, Mollero interprete, lector, Dimidius nondum, quem totum forsitan olim, (Fauerit inceptis si tantis numen amicum) Cernemus simul, atque simul mirabimur omnes.

Ergo noui (dices) quidnam nouus afferet iste Interpres? nil nempe noui, sed vetera omnia sacris Qua deprompta cadis sincero [fina?] palato Sola placent, mentemque leuant quae sola iacent, Cauponum miris quae corrupta artibus, ista Quum melior, miserante Deo, iam coeperit atas Expurgare, suo tandem reddenda nitori: En multos inter, quorum tam multa fideli Hoc nobis in opus sunt desudata labore, Nunc Mollerus adest, reliquos atate sequutus, Ingenio haud impar (quod & ipse fatebere) mult[?] Iudicio & docta nulli pietate secundus. main_text.head: IOANNI TAGAVTIO ἀντί-δωρον pro Philomelae poemate.
Sylua. VIII.
main_text.p: SAEpe quidē noctis tacitas audita per umbras, Vere nouo, Bezam miro philomela canore, Tot gracili tenuit mirantem in gutture voces: sed tenuit solo Bezam philomela canore. Quū breue nunc longo, graue nunc misceret acuto, Nunc fuscum claro, plenis exilia nctens, Nunc mire inflexas profundens gutture voces: Produ-

page.notes: The top line of the first poem is partly cut off at the right edge; "(ru" at the end of the last line is a fragment of the cut-off line. The word "fina" in line 6 and "mult" at the edge are doubtful. The Greek heading is split across two lines ("ἀντί-" / "δωρον") and was reconstructed. Line 4 of the second poem, "nctens", is doubtful. "Produ-" at the foot is a word broken at the page end.
